```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, comment = "#>")
options(width = 80, tibble.print_max = 3, tibble.print_min = 3, pillar.sigfig = 4)
library(tidyverse)
```

For each task: the code, its output, and what to look for. Where a whole table would print,
`|> nrow()` is added so that only the row count shows; your own output is the
full table, whose first line gives the same count. Where the answer is in a column that
the printout hides, `|> glimpse()` shows every column of the top rows.

Install each package once per computer; load it in every session.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
install.packages("tidyverse")
install.packages("nycflights13")
```

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(nycflights13)
```

## Task 1: operators and the pipe

a. All three are FALSE. `3 == 4` is FALSE and AND needs both. `"EWR"` is not in the set.
`10 < 20` is TRUE and NOT flips it.

```{r}
5 > 2 & 3 == 4
"EWR" %in% c("JFK", "LGA")
!(10 < 20)
```

b. The pipe puts the thing on the left into the first argument on the right. In words:
the flights, then count the rows; the flights, then keep those going to Boston.

```{r}
flights |> nrow()
flights |> filter(dest == "BOS") |> nrow()
```

## Task 2: filter, one condition

```{r}
flights |> filter(month == 12) |> nrow()          # a
flights |> filter(arr_delay > 60) |> nrow()       # b
flights |> filter(is.na(arr_delay)) |> nrow()     # c
```

c. None of these 9,430 flights has an `air_time`. They were cancelled or diverted to
another airport, so no arrival delay could be recorded. Most of them (8,713) have no
`arr_time` either.

## Task 3: filter, several conditions

```{r}
flights |> filter(dest == "BOS" | dest == "DCA") |> nrow()               # a
flights |> filter(dest %in% c("BOS", "DCA")) |> nrow()                   # a, shorter
flights |> filter(month %in% 6:8 & origin == "JFK") |> nrow()            # b
flights |> filter(arr_delay > 120 & dep_delay <= 0) |> nrow()            # c
flights |> filter(dep_delay >= 60 & dep_delay - arr_delay > 30) |> nrow() # d
```

d. Time made up in the air is `dep_delay - arr_delay`. A subtraction is allowed inside
a condition.

## Task 4: the two mistakes

a. R stops with "We detected a named input. This usually means that you've used `=`
instead of `==`." It wanted `month == 12`.

```{r, error=TRUE}
flights |> filter(month = 12)
```

b. All 336,776 rows come back. R reads `month == 12 | 1` as `(month == 12) | 1`, and
the number 1 counts as TRUE, so the condition is TRUE for every row. What was meant
gives 55,139 rows.

```{r}
flights |> filter(month == 12 | 1) |> nrow()
flights |> filter(month == 12 | month == 1) |> nrow()
flights |> filter(month %in% c(12, 1)) |> nrow()
```

## Task 5: arrange

a. Hawaiian Airlines (HA) to Honolulu on 9 January, 1,272 minutes late on arrival. The
`carrier` and `dest` columns are hidden in the normal printout; `glimpse()` shows them.

```{r}
flights |> arrange(desc(arr_delay)) |> head(10) |> glimpse()
```

b. `dep_time` 1 is 00:01, one minute past midnight. Times are stored as hhmm numbers:
517 is 05:17, 2400 is midnight.

```{r}
flights |> arrange(dep_time)
```

c. Newark to LaGuardia, 17 miles, a single flight that was cancelled. After it, Newark to
Philadelphia, 80 miles.

```{r}
flights |> arrange(distance) |> head(3) |> glimpse()
```

d. All ten go to Honolulu (HNL), the longest route, 11 hours and more in the air.

```{r}
flights |> arrange(desc(air_time)) |> head(10) |> glimpse()
```

## Task 6: distinct and count

```{r}
flights |> distinct(carrier) |> nrow()            # a: 16 airlines
flights |> distinct(dest) |> nrow()               #    105 destinations
flights |> count(carrier, sort = TRUE)            # b: United (UA) first
flights |> distinct(year, month, day) |> nrow()   # c: 365, a flight on every day
flights |> count(origin, sort = TRUE)             # d: Newark (EWR) first
```

e. The result is the same either way. Filtering first is faster: the sort then handles
28,135 rows instead of 336,776.

```{r}
flights |> filter(month == 12) |> arrange(desc(dep_delay)) |> nrow()
flights |> arrange(desc(dep_delay)) |> filter(month == 12) |> nrow()
```

## Task 7: a pipeline you can read aloud

Take the flights, then keep December, then keep arrivals more than an hour late, then
put the worst first. The two filters can also be one: `filter(month == 12 & arr_delay > 60)`.

```{r}
december_late <- flights |>
  filter(month == 12) |>
  filter(arr_delay > 60) |>
  arrange(desc(arr_delay))
nrow(december_late)
```

## Task 8: Global Superstore

Code only; the data is not in the course folder, and the file name depends on the
download. Column names with spaces need backticks, as in `` `Customer Name` ``.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
superstore <- read_csv("data/Global_Superstore.csv")
superstore |> filter(Category == "Technology" & Discount > 0.2)   # a
superstore |> arrange(desc(Profit)) |> head(5)                   # b
superstore |> distinct(`Customer Name`) |> nrow()                # c, unique customers
superstore |> count(Region, sort = TRUE)                         # c, rows per region
```
